scope: Display-detail Robot HAT V4 for the Studio: the owner's physical board reconstructed from the owner's photographs and scans; checked geometry, poses and recipes unchanged

boardIdentity.boardCodeLocation: top silkscreen beside the GPIO pad field
boardIdentity.subRevision: unresolved: no further revision or date marking is legible in the photographs
boardIdentity.confidence: Revision V4 is legible on both faces in several frames; no other revision marking was found

frame: The adopted instructional HAT frame: x along the 85 mm edge, y along the 56 mm edge with the GPIO header at high y, z up from the PCB underside, PCB top face z = 1.6. Positions in mm.

basisClasses.datum: taken from the adopted instructional HAT (mounting bores, board plane, thickness); never changed by display work
basisClasses.scan: measured on the owner's two Object Capture scans after registration to the four datum bores (top 0.21 mm RMS, underside 0.14 mm RMS)
basisClasses.photo: measured on owner photographs rectified onto the board plane through the four datum bores (residual 0.17 mm RMS on the 40 GPIO pads)
basisClasses.standard: published connector or package standard, consistent with the photographs
basisClasses.approximate: visually estimated from the photographs; not a measurement

basis.outline: scan + photo (scan 84.8 x 56.0, underside photo 55.75 wide); modelled on the 85 x 56 datum envelope

mountingHoles.silkRings: photo (both faces); set flush into the mask, because screw heads and standoff tops bear on the board around the bores and must meet its face, as they do on the instructional HAT

basis.pads: photo (40 of 40 pads matched, 0.17 mm RMS)
basis.socketDepth: scan (15.44 mm raw, 15.75 mm at the bore-fitted scale), set to 15.5 mm: the 18 mm standoffs less the Pi's 2.5 mm header base, so the socket rests on the base

basis.pitch: standard 2.54, confirmed by the underside joint lattices (0.07 to 0.14 mm mean residual)
basis.heights: standard (2.5 mm plastic, 6.0 mm mating), consistent with the low-angle photographs

servo.basis: photo + scan lattice fit; colours from the photographs

headers.basis: photo (joint positions on the rectified underside photo) + silkscreen labels

basis.housing: standard JST XH 2-pin vertical, height consistent with the scan (6.5 to 6.9 mm)
scan (x -1.0 to 6.1, top 7.2 to 7.5) + standard JST XH 3-pin side entry

basis.construction: photo (cream side-entry receptacle with a white two-wire plug)

basis.position: scan (x 19.5 to 27.8, y -2.1 to 5.3, top 4.7) + photo (shell tabs)
basis.body: standard USB Type-C receptacle shell 8.94 x 3.26

basis.position: scan (x -0.6 to 4.9, y 18.1 to 28.6, top 5.0, slider 6.2)

basis.body: approximate tactile switch 3.9 x 3.3 with a beige stadium actuator

ics.basis: photo (bodies and lead rows on the rectified top photo and close-ups) + standard package outlines; markings read from close-ups are recorded, not modelled

basis.height: scan (L2 top 5.2 to 5.3, L1 top 4.2 to 4.3)

basis.footprint: scan (top at z 8.4 to 8.9 over x 65.3 to 85.9, y 12.9 to 43.0; corner radius from the profile)

leads.basis: approximate: the speaker lead routing as photographed (J20 plug to the speaker on top; a twisted pair through the cable slot and along the underside to the notch)

passives.basis: photo (every body located on the rectified top photo at 0.5 mm grid; chip sizes snapped to 0603, 0805 and 1206; larger parts confirmed by scan height)

silkscreen.basis: photo (lettering read from the owner photographs; only legible markings are reproduced, micro-print reference designators of passives are omitted). A label with a sixth field is scaled to that photographed glyph box [x0, x1, y0, y1], because the board's typeface is narrower and taller than DejaVu
silkscreen.font: DejaVu Sans Bold from the frozen M4 environment (matplotlib data), regular for the underside slogan lines

photoComparison.basis: registered orthographic renders of the Studio-tolerance meshes (hat_review_render.py --registered: 40 px/mm over x -8..96, y -14..70) against owner photographs rectified onto the board plane through the four datum bores; features are the dark or saturated pixels inside the board; edge distances in mm. Overlays and rectified photographs stay local and are deleted after use
photoComparison.reading: Every modelled edge lies on a photographed feature (p90 under 0.5 mm on both faces). The photo-only edges on top are the unmodelled micro-print reference designators and via fields. On the underside 38 % of photo edges sit more than 3 mm from any model feature: they are the dark cores of the through-hole joints, the bore rims and the USB-C tab holes, which the model has at those positions (joint lattices 0.07 to 0.14 mm) but renders as bright tin, so the feature mask finds nothing there

preserve: Board plane, thickness and local frame
All closure poses and approach recipes
Zero HAT's existing 180 degree relation to the Pi 5 HAT pose
limitations: No caliper measurements yet: every dimension is datum, scan, photo, standard or approximate as labelled; measuredByCaliper is empty

The display GPIO socket and pad field follow the photographs (pads centred at y 52.5); the instructional HAT's schematic socket (y 47.6 to 52.6, 10 mm deep) is unchanged and remains what assembly checks use

The display overlap rows with the Pi 5 and Zero 2 W are the photographed socket engaging those boards' solid 8 mm GPIO header proxies (the real pins enter the socket about 6 mm); the M2.5 x 6 screw contacts with the board around the bores are the same 40 rows (0.03 to 2.6 mm3) the outline display recorded
IC markings, passive reference designators, via fields and the copper traces seen through the mask are not modelled; package outlines are standard sizes placed on the photographed bodies
The speaker lead routing is approximate and shows one photographed state of a flexible cable
Overlap checks compare the displayed HAT with other instructional artifacts, not pairs of detailed display models
No physical fit, electrical, installation sweep, engineering or M7 acceptance claim
